chapter: Tatum, Wiggins and Los Angeles friends
title: Frank Sebastian and Lionel Hampton's first vibes solo on "Memories"
summary: Callender tells how Sebastian brought Armstrong west and how Hampton first played vibes on Armstrong's "Memories", then that he played briefly with Hampton at the Cotton Club in 1937.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Frank Sebastian was a typical Italian, who happened to... I guess he just dug Black musicians, because that was... His house band was a Black band, and that was during a time in history when it really wasn't that popular. He's the one who brought Louis Armstrong to the Coast -- I guess you know that.

That's how Louis and Lionel Hampton got together on... Lionel Hampton made his first vibraharp date with Louis Armstrong on an arrangement of 'Memories' that Eubie Blake had sent out for Louis to record. They happened to be in the studio, and there was a vibraharp sitting

around. Of course, Lionel had never played one, or maybe he'd never seen one before, but he had been playing the orchestra bells, so the instrument itself was really no mystery to him. And Louis said, "Hey, can you play that?" (Chops, I called him). But Lionel went over and... This is a story from the horse's mouth, Lionel's mouth. Lionel went over and made an introduction in E-flat, and that's how "Memories" got recorded. Did you know that?

No, I didn't know that. I've never read it anywhere or heard it. I know that that was its first recording. But I didn't know the circumstances, and I certainly didn't know that was the first time he played the vibes.
Well, that's how it happened. It was the first time. They happened to be in the...

The studio. They belonged in the studio. The studio used them to make the radio station breaks with. So that's how Lionel Hampton played his first vibraphone solo on a record, or anywhere else, was with Louis. And the rest is history.
This was in the early Thirties, before I ever got here. When I played in Lionel's band, it was 1937,
I think -- briefly. It was in the... It was Cotton Club then, before it became the Casa Mañana.
